newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen defends Ranariddh's overthrow.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen defends Ranariddh's overthrow.

text.p: Cambodia's co-prime minister Hun Sen on Thursday accused his ousted rival Prince Norodom Ranariddh of provoking his own overthrow through a year-long "reckless strategy of provocation".

Foreign ministers from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) decided at an emergency meeting in Malaysia on Thursday to postpone Cambodia's membership in the grouping, Malaysia's national news agency Bernama said. In Phnom Penh, the foreign ministry now controlled by Hun Sen said Ranariddh had destabilised Cambodia by openly criticising Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's political party, building up his armed forces and weapons stocks, conducting secret negotiations with Khmer Rouge rebels and forming a political alliance that included the Khmer Rouge.

"Although Prince Norodom Ranariddh and his associates claim to be victims of provocation, in fact, for the past year, they have embarked on a reckless strategy of provocation, which has only served to destabilise Cambodia," the foreign ministry said in a white paper obtained by Reuters on Thursday.
ASEAN was due to induct Cambodia, along with Burma and Laos as final members of the seven-nation group at its annual meeting at the end of the month.

The foreign ministry's white paper accused Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party of trying to strengthen its faltering political position by creating a crisis in which Hun Sen would make a mistake that benefitted Ranariddh.
The Cambodian capital was tense on Thursday as foreigners scrambled to get out of the country and supporters of Ranariddh's party were either fleeing or falling in line with the new regime.

Ranariddh was ousted by the powerful Hun Sen on Sunday as Hun Sen's forces pushed royalist soldiers out of the capital in fierce fighting. The prince, in France at the time of the coup, later said he would organise a resistance to Hun Sen.

Cambodia's ambassador to the United Nations, a Ranariddh loyalist, said on Wednesday in New York that the prince's forces would capture Battambang, the country's second largest city, and set up an alternative government there.

But Thai army and Khmer Rouge guerrilla sources said on Thursday that royalist forces had agreed a ceasefire with Hun Sen's troops in western Cambodia after failing to enlist the support of ex-Khmer Rouge remnants in the area.

A military official loyal to Hun Sen told Reuters from the town on Thursday the situation there was quiet, while in Phnom Penh the government said it would fly diplomats and journalists to Battambang and Siem Reap so they could assess the situation for themselves.

Thai army sources based in eastern Thailand's Aranyaprathet bordering Cambodia's Poipet town confirmed the reports of negotiations between the rival premiers' forces and said the situation was relatively calm.
"I think Ranariddh loyalist soldiers are not in a position to hold on for more than a couple of days, so they sought to negotiate," an army source said.
Nervous FUNCINPEC party officials continued leaving the country on Thursday in the aftermath of the arrest and execution of a senior party member on Monday.
Ho Sok, a secretary of state in the interior ministry, was arrested by Hun Sen's troops on Monday and later shot dead, government officials said.

Hun Sen had earlier blamed Ho Sok and three other senior FUNCINPEC members for the weekend's fighting and said they all had to be hunted down and arrested. A FUNCINPEC intelligence officer, Chao Sambath, was among the four. There were unconfirmed reports that he had also been arrested and killed, and a newspaper which supports Hun Sen reported on Thursday that he had committed suicide.
The same newspaper reported that Ho Sok had killed himself though officials later said he had been shot dead by soldiers.

But while some royalists fled the country, others were cooperating with the new regime. Several prominent FUNCINPEC officials, including at least two ministers, attended Hun Sen's first cabinet meeting as sole prime minister on Thursday.
Hun Sen said earlier he wanted FUNCINPEC to nominate a new person to fill Ranariddh's job as First Prime Minister.

Khieu Kanharith, secretary of state for information, told reporters foreign minister Ung Huot, a FUNCINPEC member, was due to return to Cambodia within days from Paris, where he had been attending a meeting of international donors to the country.
Co-defence minister Tea Charath was also due back in the country soon, he said.

The United States said on Wednesday it was pulling out about 40 diplomats and their dependants from Cambodia and also urged all Americans to leave within days. There were between 1,000 and 1,300 Americans in the country, a U.S. official said.

Anxious Americans and other foreigners jammed information desks at a central Phnom Penh hotel and airline ticket offices in the city on Thursday, demanding seats on heavily-booked commercial and charter flights out of the city.
Cambodia's southeast Asian neighbours continued evacuating their nationals on Thursday and Australia said it, too, would evacuate its citizens.
